entries.x: One business process per journey. Each lane is a role on the personas page; each task names the skill that performs it. The BPMN source of each process is in input/business-processes/ , and a diagram viewer for each is on the harness site. Process Lanes BPMN --- --- --- J1 Issue the newborn's birth-dose DVCs in Country A Caregiver, Birth clinic vaccinator, Birth clinic issuing system, Issuer signing key j1-birth-dose-dvc.bpmn J2 Discover and refer an unregistered infant in Country B Caregiver, Community health worker, CHW app j2-chw-discovery-referral.bpmn J3 Verify, import and schedule at the home clinic Caregiver, Home clinic provider, Home clinic EHR j3-clinic-verification-schedule.bpmn J4.0 Issue the family's records to one phone as VHLs Caregiver, National health portal, Issuer signing key, Family phone j4-0-family-vhl-issuance.bpmn J4.1 Read a family member's records at the point of care abroad Caregiver, Family phone, Point-of-care provider, Point-of-care receiver j4-1-vhl-point-of-care.bpmn J1 Issue the newborn's birth-dose DVCs in Country A Process id Process J1BirthDoseDvc . View the diagram. J1, Cross-border birth and initial vaccination. In Country A (XXR, the birth country) the provincial hospital gives Chanthala's Hep B and BCG birth doses and issues one signed DVC per dose (DVCMinPreQual at subclaim -6) as a paper QR: the guide's QR Code Generation section 12 example. The hospital system is the Issuer (SMART Trust) and the HCERT side of the VHL Sharer; the private key stays with the key holder (two-phase signing, STT-ISS-004, STT-COS-006). XXR's DSC, under its CSCA, being on the GDHCN trust list is a PRECONDITION of issuing, declared below, not a step. Mali is the Holder (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw) and VHL Holder (IHE ITI VHL). Task checklist: j1-birth-dose-dvc.checklist.md. J2 Discover and refer an unregistered infant in Country B Process id Process J2ChwDiscovery . View the diagram. J2, Return home, CHW discovery and referral. Back in Country B (home, XXH), where the family resides, the community health worker finds Chanthala unregistered on a home visit. Offline, the CHW app reads the foreign DVCs without verifying them (read-unverified, STT-VER-011: the triage read stops before the trust lookup and marks every field unverified), registers the infant and refers her to the clinic for verification. The CHW app is a Receiver (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw) that deliberately stops before trust; Mali provides the VDHC as Holder (smart-trust-phw requirement provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver). Task checklist: j2-chw-discovery-referral.checklist.md. J3 Verify, import and schedule at the home clinic Process id Process J3ClinicVerification . View the diagram. J3, Clinic verification and schedule generation, in Country B. The clinic EHR (Receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, VHL Receiver side in IHE ITI VHL) holds a copy of the GDHCN trust list, which the trust anchor (Trust Network Anchor; IHE Trust Anchor) distributes and Country B, a Trust Network Participant, retrieves (smart-trust-phw retrieve-pki-material). Loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, not a step in it: the clinic may be offline throughout, so the list it verifies against is the one it last refreshed, about weekly, when the CHW visits the base clinic or district health office. It verifies each foreign DVC in the STT-VER-001 order against XXR's DSC DID document, imports the verified doses and evaluates the national schedule, which finds birth-dose OPV due. Task checklist: j3-clinic-verification-schedule.checklist.md. J4.0 Issue the family's records to one phone as VHLs Process id Process J40FamilyVhl . View the diagram. J4.0, Outbound family travel, "One Family, One Phone". Before travelling, Mali asks Country B's national portal for each family member's records. The portal, a VHL Sharer (IHE ITI VHL) and Issuer (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw), issues one passcode-protected Verifiable Health Link per member: the documents (IPS, DVCs) encrypted as JWE (STT-VHL-007) behind an ITI-YY5 manifest, the link in the SMART Health Links payload format at HCERT key 5 (STT-VHL-001, STT-VHL-002), signed with Country B's DSC. The shared phone holds the QRs for Mali, the VHL Holder. Task checklist: j4-0-family-vhl-issuance.checklist.md. J4.1 Read a family member's records at the point of care abroad Process id Process J41VhlFetch . View the diagram. J4.1. Abroad, Chanthala needs care. Mali, the VHL Holder (IHE ITI VHL; Holder in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, requirement provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver), opens her QR on the family phone and tells the passcode. The hospital system, a VHL Receiver (Receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw), verifies the HCERT against the GDHCN trust list, requests the manifest by ITI-YY5 with an HTTP Message Signature (STT-VHL-005, STT-VHL-006, STT-VHL-008) and decrypts the documents (STT-VHL-007). If the HCERT does not verify, there is no digital verification: the VHL is not followed and the records are treated like paper. As in J3, loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, not a step in it: the hospital verifies against its cached copy of the trust list and needs no connection to do so. It refreshes that cache nightly or hourly, where an offline site such as the J3 clinic refreshes about weekly. Task checklist: j4-1-vhl-point-of-care.checklist.md.

The business requirements of the journeys: who takes part (generic personas), what they want (user scenarios), how the work flows (business processes), and what the systems must do (functional requirements).
0.1.0 (ci-build) First L2 and L3 content: generic personas and system actors as ActorDefinition s, user scenarios, and the business processes J1 to J4.1, generated from the harness sources.

The system actors of the journeys and the actor definitions of WHO SMART Trust, WHO SMART Trust PHW and IHE ITI VHL each is derived from. The data the journeys exchange (DVCs as HCERTs, VHL manifests, IPS documents) is defined by those guides.

The journeys do not restate requirements. Each step of a user scenario names the requirement it exercises by its id (for example STT-VER-011 , read without verifying, in J2). Those requirements are defined, with their tests, in smart-trust-tools, which traces them to WHO SMART Trust and IHE ITI VHL. The WHO SMART Trust PHW requirements map onto the journeys as follows: provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver (Holder): J2, J3 and J4.1. receive-a-vhl (Receiver): J2, J3 and J4.1. publish- , receive- , distribute- and retrieve-pki-material : the trust anchor and the participants, preconditions of J1, J3, J4.0 and J4.1.

This guide is the WHO SMART Guidelines L2 digital adaptation kit (DAK) and L3 implementation guide of the SMART Trust demonstrator. It follows one family across borders through four journeys: Journey Where --- --- --- J1 Issue the newborn's birth-dose DVCs Country A (XXR) J2 Discover and refer an unregistered infant Country B (home) J3 Verify, import and schedule at the home clinic Country B (home) J4.0 Issue the family's records to one phone as VHLs Country B (home) J4.1 Read a family member's records at the point of care abroad abroad The journeys exercise the HCERT and VHL libraries of smart-trust-tools against WHO SMART Trust and WHO SMART Trust PHW. Every person in them is fictional. Generic personas and system actors: the roles that play each process lane. User scenarios: the user stories and the journeys step by step. Business processes: one BPMN process per journey. Functional requirements: where the journeys' requirements are defined. The source is litlfred/smart-trust-demo. This guide is a demonstrator, not WHO guidance.

These are the generic personas of the journeys J1 to J4: the roles that play the lanes of the business processes, each defined as an ActorDefinition . The people and systems that play them in the journeys are fictional. User stories Role I want to So that --- --- --- Caregiver Have my daughter's birth doses recognised at home they are not repeated and she stays on schedule Caregiver Show every family member's records abroad from one phone with one passcode each a doctor abroad can treat us without paper or an app Birth clinic vaccinator Print a signed record of each birth dose the family can carry anywhere Community health worker Read a foreign vaccination QR offline and register the child with it the clinic sees what was given before the family arrives Community health worker Refer a child whose foreign record needs checking verification is done by someone who can Home clinic provider Know whether a foreign certificate is genuine, and why not when it is not Home clinic provider See which doses are due once the foreign doses are imported I give only what is missing Point-of-care provider Read a visiting child's summary and vaccinations from a QR the parent shows without installing anything or calling another country User scenarios Each step names the requirements of smart-trust-tools it exercises. The stories are in scenarios/stories.json . J1 — Cross-border birth and initial vaccination (Country A) Precondition: the issuer's DSC is on the trust list. XXR's document signer certificate (DSC), issued under XXR's Country Signing CA (CSCA), was shared with the GDHCN, the Trust Anchor, before any DVC is signed; the GDHCN publishes it as a DID document. Sharing it is not a step of issuing. A DVC signed with a key whose DSC was never shared fails every receiver's trust-list check (STT-VER-006). Mali gives birth to Chanthala on 2026-10-21 at a provincial hospital in Country A, while visiting relatives. Dr Pimchanok WATTANA gives the Hep B and BCG birth doses and records them. For each dose, the hospital system does three things: 1. It builds a DVCMinPreQual payload: STT-PAY-001…005 and STT-PAY-007, with subclaim −6 (STT-SEL-003). 2. It prepares the CWT and the bytes to sign: STT-CWT-001…005, STT-ISS-004. 3. It has XXR's key sign them (STT-COS-002, STT-COS-006), then finishes the HC1 text: STT-COS-001, STT-ZIP-001, STT-B45-001, STT-HC1-001, STT-QR-001. Mali leaves with two paper DVCs. In the demo: the guide's two signed HC1 strings stand in for the hospital's output. Live issuance in the app uses a TEST-ONLY key (STT-ISS-003), whose DSC is not on the GDHCN list, so its DVCs do not verify in J3. J2 — Return home, CHW discovery and referral (Country B) Back in Country B, Sita RAI finds Chanthala missing from the household register on a home visit. Sita has no signal. She scans both QRs. The CHW app reads them with read-unverified (STT-VER-011; STT-B45-002, STT-ZIP-002, STT-CBR-003), which needs no trust list. It shows the doses, marked unverified. Sita registers Chanthala and refers her to the clinic. Everything syncs that evening. J3 — Clinic verification and schedule generation (Country B) Precondition: the DID documents are already loaded. Loading them is not a step of this visit. The clinic may be offline all day, so the EHR fetches nothing during it: its trust store holds the GDHCN DEV trust list as it was last refreshed, including XXR's DSC DID document (STT-TRU-001, STT-TRU-002, STT-TRU-005). A clinic with no connection of its own refreshes it about weekly, when the CHW visits the base clinic or district health office, where Country B retrieves the list the GDHCN trust anchor distributes. A DSC published after that refresh is not in the clinic's copy, so its DVC fails the trust-list check (STT-VER-006) until the next refresh. Tomas ALVES opens the referral and scans the QRs. The EHR verifies each DVC offline against that copy (STT-VER-001…009, STT-KID-002). Both verify, so it imports them as FHIR Immunization s with provenance (STT-VER-007, STT-VER-008). The national schedule then runs: the birth doses count, and birth-dose OPV is due. Tomas gives it. If a DVC fails, the EHR names the step and the reason, and Tomas decides by national policy. J4.0 — "One Family, One Phone" (Country B) Precondition, as in J1: Country B's DSC, under Country B's CSCA, is already shared with the GDHCN, the Trust Anchor. That is what lets the hospital abroad verify the link in J4.1. The family plans a trip. On the national portal, Mali asks for each member's records. For each member, the portal does three things: 1. It assembles an IPS and that member's DVCs. 2. It encrypts them (STT-VHL-004, STT-VHL-007) behind a passcode-protected manifest with an expiry (STT-VHL-009). 3. It issues the link as an HCERT, with the VHL at key 5 (STT-VHL-001, STT-VHL-002), signed with Country B's DSC. The shared phone holds one QR per member. J4.1 — Point of care abroad Precondition, as in J3: the DID documents are already loaded. The hospital system's trust store is a cached copy of the GDHCN trust list, including Country B's DSC DID document (STT-TRU-001, STT-TRU-002, STT-TRU-005). The hospital refreshes it nightly or hourly, against about weekly at the offline J3 clinic. It does not need to be online to verify: verifying reads the cache and never fetches the list. A DSC published after the last refresh fails the trust-list check (STT-VER-006), naming that reason. Abroad, Chanthala has a fever. Mali shows Chanthala's QR on the family phone and tells Dr Ana MOREIRA the passcode. The hospital system takes four steps: 1. It verifies the HCERT against Country B's DSC in that copy of the trust list. 2. It requests the manifest by ITI-YY5, signed with HTTP Message Signatures (STT-VHL-005, STT-VHL-006, STT-VHL-008). 3. It decrypts the IPS and DVCs (STT-VHL-007). 4. It shows them to Dr Ana MOREIRA. If the HCERT does not verify (for example, Country B's DSC is missing from the cached list), there is no digital verification. The hospital names the step and the reason (STT-VER-008), does not follow the VHL, and Dr Ana MOREIRA treats whatever the family can show as she would a paper record.
